title: Gullstone Solar — edge inference intake (scratch notes)
content:
Meeting capture (11/07/2025 initial intake, follow-ups 12/02, 02/18):

Quick summary:
- Customer: Gullstone Solar (off-grid microgrid operator). Use case: sensor anomaly detection + lightweight summarization for field techs.
- Desired outcome: run an anomaly-detection model near the array controller (edge aggregator) with occasional batched upload of condensed telemetry to central service.
- Constraints: intermittent WAN, limited edge GPU/CPU budget, strict customer policy for PII-free telemetry, on-prem/private control plane required.

Notes from call:
- 5 regional sites to start, target scale 50 sites in 6 months. Each site: 1 ARM gateway (4 CPU cores, 8GB RAM) + aggregator rack (1x small GPU, ~12GB VRAM) that can host Redwood Private aggregator.
- SLOs: 95th latency < 200ms for single-sensor anomaly inference; bulk evaluation / batch jobs can be async. Throughput target ~100 inference req/s aggregate per aggregator during peak (short bursts).
- Model quality: need >90% recall on labelled anomaly dataset (we will get their 6 months of annotated failure logs). Precision secondary but important to reduce false alarms.

Technical constraints / gotchas observed / flagged:
- Device-level time drift: logs have inconsistent timestamps; caution using prefix-caching keyed on wallclock. Need to normalize using device heartbeat stream.
- Cold-starts after power cycles are frequent; model warmup must be fast and not assume large KV cache available.
- Intermittent connectivity: aggregator must buffer requests and optionally fallback to local light heuristic (thresholding) when model unavailable.
- Quantized model ops: some operators in their training stack (custom conv variant) not supported by our off-the-shelf quant kernels -> may need kernel fallbacks or small op rework.
- KMS: customer requires HSM-backed keys for model artifacts and logs (bring-your-own-key). Confirm support path for HSM integration during Private deployment.
- Storage: local SSDs are small (100GB); need to avoid storing multiple model checkpoints on device. Use single pinned model + rolling telemetry window.

Proposed PoC architecture (initial hypothesis):
- Deploy Redwood Private control plane in their VPC (dedicated subnet).
- Run lightweight Redwood edge agent on ARM gateway for routing + buffering. Aggregator rack runs a small containerized inference node with 1x A10G or equivalent (12GB VRAM) for quantized 7B/13B variant.
- Model: try Llama-derivative 7B 8-bit quant first for memory fit, then 13B-8bit if accuracy < 90%.
- Fallback policy: on aggregator failure, route to regional hosted fallback (if customer opts in) or local heuristic. We need to confirm fallback acceptance.

Evaluation plan / metrics:
- Collect labeled dataset (Gullstone to deliver CSV + sample telemetry: timestamp, sensor_id, reading, label) by 11/21.
- Baseline: run their current rule-based detector on dataset to capture false positive/negative rates.
- PoC goal: match or exceed baseline recall, reduce FP by >20% ideally while keeping median infer latency <120ms locally.

Open questions for customer (to answer before spike):
- Confirm willingness to allow regional fallback (hosted Redwood) or must be strictly air-gapped?
- Can they provision 1 GPU per aggregator rack or do we need to consider multi-aggregator pooling?
- Are there any proprietary ops in their trained model? If yes, get model repo / Docker to test quantization pipeline.
- Do they have a preferred KMS/HSM provider (AWS CloudHSM, Azure Key Vault HSM) or an on-prem HSM?

Immediate next steps (owner / eta):
- Samir: spin up sample quantization test using their anonymized sample (if they can share) or synthetic telemetry; target: 11/14 (DONE -> initial quant test looked promising, see git PR).
- Riley: prepare infra checklist for Private PoC (VPC peering, subnet sizing, HSM options, storage plan). Draft due 11/14, review 11/18.
- Maya (me): coordinate data transfer + sign NDA addendum for telemetry; request sample dataset and example model artifact. Email sent 11/08, chasing 11/13.
- Aisha: run latency microbench on candidate quantized 7B model on small GPU instance to confirm <120ms median for single inference. ETA 11/12.

Action items after initial PoC signoff:
- Small onsite test at one site with our aggregator node for 2 weeks (monitor power-cycle behaviour, cold-starts).
- Add deterministic warmup script to agent so model warms gradually during aggregator boot without large mem spikes.
- Implement offline buffer + backpressure: store up to 24 hours of inference requests if WAN down, with retry policy.

Risks / escalation path:
- If quantization breaks custom ops, we will need model code changes or to build custom kernels — this can add 4–6 weeks. Escalate to Applied ML team (cc: Dr. Chen) early.
- HSM integration delays: involve security & compliance to scope certs and network egress rules in parallel with infra setup.

Misc notes / brain dump (notes-to-self):
- Consider tiny ensemble: local 7B quant for speed + lightweight rule-layer for precision tuning.
- Check whether caching prefixes by site makes sense given sparse repeating patterns in telemetry (likely low reuse).
- Flag: telemetry contains device serials currently; ensure PII scrubbing pipeline before any hosted uploads.

Links and refs:
- INF-4021 (Jira) for PoC ticket; Confluence page above for scope doc; github PR for quant test.

Next meeting: 11/20 sync with Gullstone engineering (confirm dataset delivery + HSM preference).

Quick TODO checklist (short):
- [ ] Confirm HSM provider (Gullstone)
- [x] Initial quantization smoke test (Samir)
- [ ] Receive labeled dataset (Gullstone)
- [ ] Finalize PoC infra checklist (Riley)
- [ ] Schedule 2-week onsite test slot

End of scratch notes.
